# Solver and Constraint Support {#sec-92-solver-matrix}

```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false
source("R/_common.R")
library(tidypm)
library(knitr)
```

Which solver honors which constraint, measured rather than transcribed. Read
alongside @sec-13-solvers-implementation, which explains why the distinction between
*accepts* and *honors* is the one that matters.

Two tables follow. The first is what the package documents: which combinations
are supported. The second is what the package does: whether the returned
portfolio actually satisfies what was asked. They do not agree, and the
disagreement is silent in every case.

```{r}
#| label: universe
R  <- as_xts_pm(sim_class_returns_monthly, date, class, return)
Re <- R - sim_riskfree_monthly$return
N  <- ncol(Re); S <- stats::cov(Re); mu <- colMeans(Re)

sol <- quadprog::solve.QP(2 * S, rep(0, N), cbind(mu, diag(N)),
                          c(1, rep(0, N)), meq = 1)
w_true <- pmax(sol$solution, 0); w_true <- setNames(w_true / sum(w_true), colnames(Re))
sharpe <- function(w) sum(mu * w) / sqrt(as.numeric(t(w) %*% S %*% w))
```

The benchmark is the long-only tangency portfolio on the sixteen risky class
series, solved directly with `quadprog` and therefore free of anything
`PortfolioAnalytics` might get wrong. Its monthly Sharpe ratio is
`r sprintf("%.4f", sharpe(w_true))`, held in `r sum(w_true > 1e-6)` positions.

## What the package documents

```{r}
#| label: tbl-90-support
#| tbl-cap: "Support as described by the package. `optimize_method` values across the top; a tick means the combination is accepted."
#| echo: false
tibble::tribble(
  ~Feature,                    ~ROI, ~CVXR, ~random, ~DEoptim, ~pso, ~GenSA,
  "minimum variance",          "yes", "yes", "yes", "yes", "yes", "yes",
  "quadratic utility",         "yes", "yes", "yes", "yes", "yes", "yes",
  "maximum Sharpe (maxSR)",    "yes", "yes", "yes", "yes", "yes", "yes",
  "minimum ES / CVaR",         "yes", "yes", "yes", "yes", "yes", "yes",
  "target return",             "yes", "yes", "yes", "yes", "yes", "yes",
  "box constraints",           "yes", "yes", "yes", "yes", "yes", "yes",
  "group constraints",         "yes", "yes", "yes", "yes", "yes", "yes",
  "turnover constraint",       "yes", "penalty", "yes", "yes", "yes", "yes",
  "proportional costs",        "yes", "no",  "yes", "yes", "yes", "yes",
  "position limit",            "max return, min ES only", "no", "yes", "yes", "yes", "yes",
  "leverage exposure",         "MILP only", "no", "yes", "yes", "yes", "yes",
  "diversification",           "no",  "no",  "yes", "yes", "yes", "yes",
  "risk budgeting",            "no",  "no",  "yes", "yes", "yes", "yes"
) |>
  kable(align = "lcccccc")
```

Three entries in that table are already misleading, and the chapters say so:
`position limit` is available under ROI **only** on the maximum-return and
minimum-ES mixed-integer paths, not on the mean-variance quadratic program;
`leverage exposure` is documented for ROI's mixed-integer path alone, but the
quadratic path accepts it and returns a long-only portfolio; and `turnover`
under CVXR is a penalty term, not a constraint, so it bends rather than binds.
A "no" in the table does not mean an error, either: the constraint is accepted
and dropped, which @tbl-90-roi measures.

## What the package does

```{r}
#| label: measured
set.seed(1602)

base <- portfolio.spec(assets = colnames(Re)) |>
  add.constraint(type = "full_investment") |>
  add.constraint(type = "long_only") |>
  add.objective(type = "return", name = "mean") |>
  add.objective(type = "risk",   name = "StdDev")

probe <- function(spec, method, max_pos = NULL, ...) {
  t0 <- Sys.time()
  o <- try(suppressWarnings(
    optimize.portfolio(Re, spec, optimize_method = method,
                       maxSR = TRUE, trace = FALSE, ...)), silent = TRUE)
  secs <- as.numeric(difftime(Sys.time(), t0, units = "secs"))
  lim <- if (is.null(max_pos)) NA_integer_ else as.integer(max_pos)
  if (inherits(o, "try-error")) {
    return(tibble::tibble(solver = method, share = NA_real_, limit = lim, holdings = NA_integer_,
                          verdict = "errors", seconds = secs))
  }
  w <- extractWeights(o)
  if (is.null(w) || anyNA(w)) {
    return(tibble::tibble(solver = method, share = NA_real_, limit = lim, holdings = NA_integer_,
                          verdict = "NA weights, silently", seconds = secs))
  }
  w <- w[colnames(Re)]; h <- sum(w > 1e-6)
  tibble::tibble(solver = method, share = sharpe(w) / sharpe(w_true), limit = lim, holdings = h,
                 verdict = if (is.null(max_pos)) "solved"
                           else if (h <= max_pos) "feasible" else "VIOLATES",
                 seconds = secs)
}

unconstrained <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  probe(base, "ROI"), probe(base, "CVXR"), probe(base, "random"),
  probe(base, "DEoptim", traceDE = 0), probe(base, "pso"), probe(base, "GenSA")
)

# A limit that binds: one position fewer than the unconstrained answer holds.
k   <- sum(w_true > 1e-6) - 1L
lim <- add.constraint(base, type = "position_limit", max_pos = k)
limited <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  probe(lim, "ROI", max_pos = k), probe(lim, "random", max_pos = k),
  probe(lim, "DEoptim", max_pos = k, traceDE = 0),
  probe(lim, "pso", max_pos = k), probe(lim, "GenSA", max_pos = k)
)
# what the text below says: ROI, pso and GenSA return more positions than the limit
stopifnot(all(limited$holdings[limited$solver %in% c("ROI", "pso", "GenSA")] > k))
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-90-unconstrained
#| tbl-cap: "The plain tangency problem, which is convex and has one answer. `share` is the fraction of the attainable Sharpe ratio reached."
#| echo: false
unconstrained |>
  dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(share)) |>
  dplyr::mutate(share = sprintf("%.1f%%", 100 * share),
                seconds = sprintf("%.0f", seconds)) |>
  dplyr::select(solver, share, holdings, verdict, seconds) |>
  kable(align = "lrrlr",
        col.names = c("", "share of the best", "positions", "verdict", "seconds"))
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-90-limited
#| tbl-cap: "The same problem with a position limit one below the number of positions the unconstrained answer holds, so that it binds. Anything above the limit in the `positions` column is an infeasible portfolio returned without complaint."
#| echo: false
limited |>
  dplyr::mutate(share = ifelse(is.na(share), "--", sprintf("%.1f%%", 100 * share)),
                holdings = ifelse(is.na(holdings), "--", as.character(holdings)),
                seconds = sprintf("%.0f", seconds)) |>
  dplyr::select(solver, share, limit, holdings, verdict, seconds) |>
  kable(align = "lrrrlr",
        col.names = c("", "share", "limit", "positions", "verdict", "seconds"))
```

The third table takes ROI alone and asks it for the three constraints that
@sec-12-constraints-implementation found it does not honor on the quadratic
path, each with a bound that binds, and for the two linear paths on which it
does honor a position limit.

```{r}
#| label: roi-constraints
roi  <- function(spec) extractWeights(optimize.portfolio(Re, spec, optimize_method = "ROI"))[colnames(Re)]
same <- function(a, b) isTRUE(all.equal(a, b))
long <- portfolio.spec(assets = colnames(Re)) |>
  add.constraint(type = "full_investment") |> add.constraint(type = "long_only")
var_obj <- function(spec) add.objective(spec, type = "risk", name = "var")
pos     <- function(spec, k) add.constraint(spec, type = "position_limit", max_pos = k)

w_mv <- roi(var_obj(long)); k_mv <- sum(w_mv > 1e-6) - 1L
w_es <- roi(long |> add.objective(type = "risk", name = "ES")); k_es <- sum(w_es > 1e-6) - 1L
# maximum return needs a cap and a class limit before fewer positions are feasible at all
grp_eq <- split(seq_len(N), ifelse(grepl("_equity$", colnames(Re)), "equity", "other"))
stopifnot(identical(names(grp_eq), c("equity", "other")))
ret_spec <- portfolio.spec(assets = colnames(Re)) |>
  add.constraint(type = "full_investment") |> add.constraint(type = "box", min = 0, max = 0.5) |>
  add.constraint(type = "group", groups = grp_eq, group_min = c(0, 0), group_max = c(0.6, 1)) |>
  add.objective(type = "return", name = "mean")
w_ret <- roi(ret_spec); k_ret <- sum(w_ret > 1e-6) - 1L
w_pos_mv  <- roi(pos(long, k_mv) |> var_obj())
w_pos_es  <- roi(pos(long, k_es) |> add.objective(type = "risk", name = "ES"))
w_pos_ret <- roi(pos(ret_spec, k_ret))
w_lev <- roi(portfolio.spec(assets = colnames(Re)) |>
  add.constraint(type = "full_investment") |> add.constraint(type = "box", min = -0.3, max = 1) |>
  add.constraint(type = "leverage_exposure", leverage = 1.6) |> var_obj())
w_div <- roi(long |> add.constraint(type = "diversification", div_target = 0.7) |> var_obj())
stopifnot(1 - sum(w_mv^2) < 0.7)                             # the target binds

held    <- function(w) sum(abs(w) > 1e-6)
verdict <- function(w, ok, w0, what = "the unconstrained weights")
  if (same(w, w0)) paste0("dropped: ", what, ", no message") else if (ok) "honored" else "VIOLATES"
roi_tbl <- tibble::tibble(
  constraint = c("position limit", "position limit", "position limit", "leverage exposure", "diversification"),
  objective  = c("minimum variance", "minimum ES", "maximum return", "minimum variance", "minimum variance"),
  asked      = c(sprintf("at most %d positions", c(k_mv, k_es, k_ret)),
                 "gross exposure at most 1.6, shorts to -30%", "1 - w'w at least 0.7"),
  returned   = c(sprintf("%d positions", c(held(w_pos_mv), held(w_pos_es), held(w_pos_ret))),
                 sprintf("gross exposure %.2f, %d short positions", sum(abs(w_lev)), sum(w_lev < -1e-6)),
                 sprintf("1 - w'w of %.2f", 1 - sum(w_div^2))),
  verdict    = c(verdict(w_pos_mv, held(w_pos_mv) <= k_mv, w_mv), verdict(w_pos_es, held(w_pos_es) <= k_es, w_es),
                 verdict(w_pos_ret, held(w_pos_ret) <= k_ret, w_ret),
                 verdict(w_lev, sum(abs(w_lev)) <= 1.6 + 1e-6, w_mv, "the long-only weights"),
                 verdict(w_div, 1 - sum(w_div^2) >= 0.7 - 1e-6, w_mv)))
# what the text below says, asserted
stopifnot(same(w_pos_mv, w_mv), held(w_pos_es) <= k_es, held(w_pos_ret) <= k_ret, same(w_lev, w_mv), same(w_div, w_mv))
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-90-roi
#| tbl-cap: "ROI on the build this book pins: three constraints on the quadratic path, each with a bound that binds, and the position limit on the two mixed-integer paths. No call raised an error, a warning or a message."
#| echo: false
kable(roi_tbl, align = "lllll", col.names = c("constraint", "objective", "asked", "returned", "verdict"))
```

## The gaps worth knowing

**Position limits on the quadratic path.** No cardinality formulation exists,
so the constraint cannot be honored. On the build this book pins, a position
limit (`max_pos`) on ROI's quadratic path is dropped without a message: no
error, no warning, and the unconstrained weights come back, exactly as on the
CRAN release. ROI honors the limit only on its two mixed-integer paths, maximum
return and minimum expected shortfall, which it hands to `Rglpk`. A patch that
refuses the quadratic call is proposed upstream, not in the pinned build. See
@sec-93-package-notes.

**Leverage exposure on the quadratic path.** `gmv_opt_leverage()` builds its
`ROI::OP()` without the variable bounds that `gmv_opt()` passes, so ROI's
default of $x \ge 0$ overrules the box and the long-only minimum-variance
portfolio comes back, with gross exposure of one. Under CVXR the constraint is
not written at all. @sec-12-constraints-implementation solves the same problem
by hand.

**`pso` and `GenSA` under a position limit.** Both accept the constraint and
return portfolios of `r limited$holdings[limited$solver == "pso"]` and
`r limited$holdings[limited$solver == "GenSA"]` positions against a limit of
`r k`, most or all of the universe. This is not a convergence failure — the
search never encoded the restriction.

**An exact `full_investment` constraint.** On the CRAN release, `min_sum ==
max_sum` is written as two opposing inequality rows, which quadprog reports as
infeasible; ROI then returns `NA` weights without raising. Measured with the
CRAN release on dataset 6.2.0, as @sec-09-mean-variance-implementation does,
30 of 312 rolling sixty-month minimum-variance windows fail this way; the
build this book pins carries the fix (@sec-93-package-notes). The
metaheuristics meet the same constraint differently, warning that it is
"restrictive" and advising `min_sum = 0.99, max_sum = 1.01` — which is advice to
leave a percent of the portfolio uninvested in order to make a solver comfortable.

**Solver names under CVXR.** Dispatch happens on the *second* element of
`optimize_method`, matched against a hard-coded list. `CLARABEL` is installed, is
CVXR's own default, and is not on the list; asking for it returns an object with
no weights and no error. See @sec-09-mean-variance-implementation.

**Risk budgeting and diversification.** Neither has a convex formulation here.
Under ROI a diversification target is accepted and ignored without a message,
as @tbl-90-roi shows, so every result in @sec-14-risk-based-allocation-theory
and every diversification floor comes from a search whose accuracy
@tbl-90-unconstrained measures.

## How to read all of this

The single practical conclusion, and it is the one @sec-13-solvers-implementation ends
on: **audit the answer.** Check that the weights sum to what you asked, that none
is negative under a long-only constraint, and that the number of positions
respects the limit. Four lines, run every time, and they catch every failure
tabulated above.
